cues.en: Instructor: Now, I haven't really stressed this term here, Pearson correlation.
cues.zh: 講師：我一直沒有特別強調「皮爾森相關」這個詞。

cues.en: But it turns out that all of the correlations that you've been learning about so far in this section are all one specific type of a correlation coefficient
cues.zh: 其實到目前為止，本單元學到的所有相關，都屬於某一種特定的相關係數，

cues.en: and that is called the Pearson correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 叫作皮爾森相關係數。

cues.en: It's called this because it's named after Pearson, who was one of the most prolific and influential statisticians.
cues.zh: 這個名稱來自 Pearson，他是產出最豐富、影響力最大的統計學家之一。

cues.en: We owe a lot of modern inferential statistics to this guy, Pearson.
cues.zh: 許多現代推論統計，都要歸功於 Pearson。

cues.en: But there are other kinds of correlation coefficients.
cues.zh: 不過，還有其他種類的相關係數。

cues.en: In fact, there are three that I'm going to teach you in this course.
cues.zh: 這門課其實會教三種。

cues.en: One of them is Pearson, which you've already learned.
cues.zh: 其中一種是已經學過的皮爾森相關。

cues.en: Another one is Spearman, and another one is Kendall's correlation.
cues.zh: 另外兩種是史皮爾曼相關與肯德爾相關。

cues.en: Okay, so to set this up, why we need to have these alternative methods for computing correlations, I'm going to highlight a few problems
cues.zh: 為了說明為什麼需要其他相關計算方法，我要凸顯皮爾森相關係數

cues.en: with the Pearson correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 的一些問題。

cues.en: And that's basically really nicely illustrated by this set of numbers of pairs, and it's called Anscobe's quartet because there's another guy Anscobe
cues.zh: 這組成對數字可以很清楚地示範，稱為安斯康姆 四重奏，因為另一位名叫 Anscombe 的人，

cues.en: who came up with these remarkable illustrations.
cues.zh: 設計了這些很精彩的例子。

cues.en: So we have here is four different variables, four different sets of variable pairs where the correlation is exactly the same.
cues.zh: 這裡有四個不同變數，或者說四組不同的變數配對，相關卻完全相同。

cues.en: So this is r sub p is the Pearson correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: r 下標 p 代表皮爾森相關係數。

cues.en: So the Pearson correlation coefficient is 0.82, 0.82, 0.82, and 0.82.
cues.zh: 四個皮爾森相關係數分別是 0.82、0.82、0.82 與 0.82。

cues.en: Now here in this case, this looks, you know, this is kind of the good scenario, the correlation coefficient is 0.8, and we see that there's a really
cues.zh: 這裡是比較理想的情況，相關係數為 0.8，可以看到這兩個變數之間，

cues.en: nice, strong linear relationship between these two variables here.
cues.zh: 有很清楚、很強的線性關係。

cues.en: Now here is another weird case because if you look at this correlation, it actually looks like the two variables are really, really strongly correlated with each other.
cues.zh: 這邊是另一種奇怪的情況，因為看起來兩個變數其實非常強相關。

cues.en: In the sense that if I gave you the value of X, you could tell me exactly what is the value of Y.
cues.zh: 意思是，如果給你 X 值，你就能精確告訴我 Y 值。

cues.en: It's based on some, you know, there's some quadratic formula or something like that.
cues.zh: 它基於某種二次公式之類的關係。

cues.en: But the Pearson correlation coefficient defines this line that goes through these dots, and this does not seem to be the right way to fit these data, right?
cues.zh: 但皮爾森相關定義的是通過這些點的直線，這似乎不是擬合資料的正確方式，對吧？

cues.en: I think we can all agree that this line is not the best way to represent the relationship between X and Y.
cues.zh: 我想我們都同意，這條直線不是呈現 X 與 Y 關係的最佳方式。

cues.en: Nonetheless, this is the Pearson correlation between these two, and it is 0.82, exactly the same magnitude of a correlation as in this example.
cues.zh: 儘管如此，兩者的皮爾森相關是 0.82，與這個例子的相關大小完全相同。

cues.en: Now, don't, so this is a problem that we cannot solve using simple correlations.
cues.zh: 這是無法用簡單相關解決的問題。

cues.en: Later on in the course, in the section on regression, you'll learn about polynomial regression.
cues.zh: 課程稍後在迴歸單元中，會學到多項式迴歸。

cues.en: And so don't worry, there is a really great way to capture this kind of a relationship, but the correlation coefficient is not really great at it.
cues.zh: 所以不用擔心，有很好的方法能捕捉這類關係，但相關係數不太擅長。

cues.en: And why is that the case?
cues.zh: 為什麼會這樣？

cues.en: Why is the correlation coefficient not doing a good job at capturing this relationship?
cues.zh: 為什麼相關係數無法好好捕捉這個關係？

cues.en: Well, you might remember from the first video in this section that I said that the correlation coefficient measures the linear relationship between two variables.
cues.zh: 你可能記得，本單元第一支影片說過，相關係數衡量的是兩個變數的線性關係。

cues.en: And in fact, I gave you that example of data that were organized into a circle, and the correlation was zero.
cues.zh: 當時也舉了資料排列成圓形、相關為 0 的例子。

cues.en: So the real relationship between X and Y is a non-linear relationship.
cues.zh: X 與 Y 的真正關係，其實是非線性的。

cues.en: There's some kind of squared term in here that's creating a non-linearity.
cues.zh: 某個平方項造成了非線性。

cues.en: And what the Pearson correlation is actually getting or latching onto here is the linear component of that relationship.
cues.zh: 皮爾森相關在這裡實際抓到的，是那個關係中的線性成分。

cues.en: So in some sense, the Pearson correlation isn't wrong per se, but it's just not the optimal model for these data.
cues.zh: 某種程度上，皮爾森相關本身並沒有錯，只是它不是這些資料的最佳模型。

cues.en: Okay, nonetheless, here we get another situation.
cues.zh: 接著看另一種情況。

cues.en: There's almost a perfect, perfect relationship between these variables.
cues.zh: 這些變數之間幾乎是完全的關係。

cues.en: However, there's one weird point up here.
cues.zh: 不過，上面有一個奇怪的點。

cues.en: There's one outlier up here, and that outlier has quite a bit of leverage.
cues.zh: 這裡有個離群值，而且具有相當大的槓桿值。

cues.en: So the correlation turns out to be 0.82, which seems to be underrepresenting this estimate.
cues.zh: 因此，相關最後是 0.82，看起來低估了這個關係。

cues.en: So this is a clear example of an outlier having a negative impact on the estimate of the relationship here.
cues.zh: 這清楚示範了，離群值如何對關係估計造成負面影響。

cues.en: And then finally, we get to this example where the entire relationship is just driven by this one outlier over here.
cues.zh: 最後來到這個例子，整個關係完全由這一個離群值所驅動。

cues.en: All these data points are exactly aligned.
cues.zh: 所有這些資料點都精確對齊。

cues.en: So the correlation, excluding this, the correlation here is actually non-existent.
cues.zh: 排除這個點，這裡的相關其實不存在。

cues.en: There is no correlation here.
cues.zh: 這裡沒有相關。

cues.en: But we have one single point all the way out here, and that gives us a correlation of 0.82.
cues.zh: 但遠處有這一個點，就讓相關變成 0.82。

cues.en: Now what you see, the second number here is r sub s.
cues.zh: 這裡第二個數字是 r 下標 s。

cues.en: This is the Spearman correlation.
cues.zh: 這是史皮爾曼相關。

cues.en: And I'm gonna talk more about the Spearman correlation in the next video, actually.
cues.zh: 下一支影片會進一步談史皮爾曼相關。

cues.en: But for now, I just want to highlight that the Spearman correlation is the same as the Pearson correlation when the data look good, when they're normally distributed.
cues.zh: 現在只想指出，資料看起來良好、呈常態分布時，史皮爾曼相關與皮爾森相關相同。

cues.en: We get a lower Spearman correlation here, a really high Spearman correlation here, almost one.
cues.zh: 這裡史皮爾曼相關較低，這裡則非常高，幾乎是 1。

cues.en: And this one seems better.
cues.zh: 這個似乎更好。

cues.en: This seems more robust to this outlier.
cues.zh: 它似乎對這個離群值比較穩健。

cues.en: And here we get a Spearman correlation that is actually still kind of inflating this relationship here.
cues.zh: 這裡的史皮爾曼相關，其實仍然有些高估這個關係。

cues.en: Okay, but I don't wanna focus on the difference between Pearson and Spearman for right now.
cues.zh: 但目前先不聚焦皮爾森與史皮爾曼的差異。

cues.en: Instead, I want to focus on the problem with Pearson.
cues.zh: 而是聚焦皮爾森的問題。

cues.en: So the Pearson correlation coefficient can over represent or under represent, so it can be biased in a positive way or biased in a negative way.
cues.zh: 皮爾森相關係數可能高估或低估，也就是產生正向偏差或負向偏差，

cues.en: The relationships between variables, if those variables contain either non-linearities, like what you see here, or if they contain outliers, like what you see here.
cues.zh: 如果變數之間的關係有這裡看到的非線性，或有這裡看到的離群值。

cues.en: And the conclusion here is that the Pearson correlation coefficient, and again, this is the correlation coefficient you've been learning about so far in this section,
cues.zh: 因此結論是，皮爾森相關係數，也就是到目前為止本單元學到的相關係數，

cues.en: the Pearson correlation is an appropriate measure of the linear relationship between two normally distributed variables or you know, roughly normally distributed variables.
cues.zh: 適合衡量兩個常態分布，或大致常態分布變數之間的線性關係。

cues.en: If you have non-linearities, if you have strong outliers, the Pearson correlation isn't going to be a really appropriate measure.
cues.zh: 如果有非線性，或很強的離群值，皮爾森相關就不是很合適的指標。

cues.en: Now, non-linearities in data are something we have to deal with in a different way, not with correlations.
cues.zh: 資料的非線性，必須透過其他方法處理，而非相關。

cues.en: Because all kinds of correlations, or at least all the correlations I'm discussing in this section are all measuring linear relationships, but they're differently sensitive to outliers.
cues.zh: 因為所有相關，至少本單元討論的所有相關，都衡量線性關係，只是對離群值的敏感度不同。

cues.en: So we are going to need to deal with this somehow.
cues.zh: 因此，我們需要某種方式處理這個問題。

cues.en: And the way that we are going to deal with that, in particular for outliers is using the Spearman rank correlation, and that is what you'll learn about in the next video.
cues.zh: 特別是離群值，我們會使用史皮爾曼秩相關處理，這就是下一支影片要學的內容。
